title: Safety: find and prevent errors from production logs
body:
EDITED ON 26/10/2017:

> What I have in mind is a tool that would look for lines containing error or warning (by doing something similar to a tail -f mylog.out | grep error), group these lines by type of error (or warning), then send a summary every week (e.g. by email).
> 
> We don't need a fancy dashboard, just a tool that would be able to do this grouping from our log files and send us a summary.
author: Participant 1

comments.author: Participant 2
comments.body:
Is it an issue? Prod logs are great to gather technical community feedback.

Before addressing this issue, there would be a need of a modern build pipeline of scripts, it will help to whether silent errors or not, based on environment. For now, it seems to me that static files are served directly ( `whydJS/public/js` folder)

So far, I saw logs from:
- [Google Analytics](https://github.com/openwhyd/openwhyd/blob/d5935d7f1001e682174fdcba6b79cbda23e97ecc/whydJS/public/js/whydtr.js#L54)
- [jQueryMigrate, this one needs only `jQuery.migrateMute = true`](https://github.com/openwhyd/openwhyd/blob/ce1cb979bb2396b94016bda3fb3388fd20f9e402/whydJS/public/js/jquery-migrate-1.2.1.js#L17) 
- WhydPlayer, who depends from your Playem

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
I was thinking of server logs, actually.

Today, they are stored in log files on the production server, and there is no way to monitor to alert developers in case of critical errors.

Do you have any service to recommend for that?
 (Something that we could use for free, as an open source project)

comments.author: Participant 1
comments.body:
> You can also use Monit to monitor files, directories and filesystems on localhost. Monit can monitor these items for changes, such as timestamps changes, checksum changes or size changes. This is also useful for security reasons - you can monitor the md5 or sha1 checksum of files that should not change and get an alert or perform an action if they should change.

Interesting, indeed, @josselinchevalay!

Is this the right tool to aggregate warning and error messages by type, so that we can focus on the most important issues to solve first?

What I have in mind is a tool that would look for lines containing `error` or `warning` (by doing something similar to a `tail -f mylog.out | grep error`), group these lines by type of `error` (or `warning`), then send a summary every week (e.g. by email).

We don't need a fancy dashboard, just a tool that would be able to do this grouping from our log files and send us a summary.
